topic: Seatbelt retractor: why does a seatbelt lock when you yank it? (webbing-sensitive lock: a spring-held weighted lever on the spool swings out by centrifugal force and catches inward-facing teeth). Part 1; Part 2 = the vehicle sensor (pendulum/ball that locks on hard braking).
principle: The belt is wound on a spring-loaded spool; a small weighted lever on the spool is held in by a light spring, so a slow pull turns the spool freely, but a yank spins the spool fast enough that centrifugal force swings the weighted lever outward until it catches a tooth and the spool stops; when the belt is let go the rewind spring turns the spool back, the lever leaves the tooth and the spring pulls it in.

firstComment:
Answer: a tiny weighted lever 🔧

Inside the retractor, the belt is wound on a spool. On the side of the spool sits a small weighted lever, held in by a light spring.

Pull the belt slowly and the spool turns slowly: the spring keeps the lever in, so the belt runs free.

Yank it and the spool spins fast: centrifugal force swings the weighted end of the lever outward, it catches a tooth, and the spool can't turn. Locked.

Let go and a coiled rewind spring winds the belt back in.

There's a second sensor that locks the belt when the car stops suddenly, even if you don't yank it. That's Part 2.

(Simplified 3D model, slowed down: here the lever catches the fixed teeth directly; in many real retractors it trips a separate locking pawl.)

Sources:
HowStuffWorks, How Seat Belts Work (a weighted pivoting lever on the spool, held by a spring; a yank spins the spool faster and centrifugal force drives it outward; a spiral spring rewinds the spool; a pendulum locks it in a sudden stop): https://auto.howstuffworks.com/car-driving-safety/safety-regulatory-devices/seatbelt3.htm
European patent EP0761513B1 (the webbing sensor is a flyweight that moves in response to rapid rotation; it is urged into inward facing teeth of the lock plate): https://data.epo.org/publication-server/rest/v1.2/publication-dates/20000517/patents/EP0761513NWB1/document.pdf
US patent US6691943 (web sensor: an inertia member with an integral locking pawl that engages radially inward pointing teeth): https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/ec/0b/36/1b94d811a45daf/US6691943.pdf
altText: 3D animation of a seatbelt retractor: a dark belt runs up from a spool held in a steel frame with a gold front plate. Through a round hole in the plate you see a steel disc on the end of the spool with two small orange weighted levers, each held in by a little spring, and a ring of inward-pointing teeth around them. Slow pull: the spool turns slowly and the levers stay in, so the belt runs free. Yank: the spool spins fast, the levers swing outward, one catches a tooth and the spool stops. Locked. Then the spool winds back, the levers drop back in and the belt rewinds. Text on screen: Why does it lock? Slow pull: free. Yank! Locked. Fast spin = swings out. Spring winds it back.
